formation.title: The Kazakh Khanate
formation.text:
When Janibek and Kerei led their followers away from the crumbling authority of Abu'l-Khayr's Uzbek confederation, they did not merely rebel, they founded a nation. Two hundred thousand nomads chose freedom on the open steppe over submission, and from that exodus the Kazakh people were born.

Now the khanate stands at a crossroads that will define its character for generations. The Chinggisid tradition demands a strong khan who can unite the clans under a single banner, marshaling the full strength of the steppe against any foe. But the reality of the vast Desht-i Kipchak favors a different wisdom: the confederal division of the three zhuz, where each horde governs its own pastures and the khan rules by consensus with the biys and sultans.

Which path shall define the Kazakh nation?

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

options.text: One khan, one nation, as Kasym commanded

modifiers.name: Legacy of Kasym Khan
modifiers.text: Under Kasym Khan, the Kazakh Khanate reached its zenith, fielding two hundred thousand cavalry and commanding the entire Desht-i Kipchak from the Irtysh to the Ural. His centralized authority, backed by the Chinggisid mandate, forged scattered clans into a single terrifying force.

options.text: Three zhuz, one people, strength through balance

modifiers.name: Confederacy of the Three Zhuz
modifiers.text: The genius of Kazakh governance lies not in the power of a single khan but in the balance of three zhuz, the Great, Middle, and Junior hordes. Each maintains its pastures, its biys, its traditions. Unity arises from consensus, not command, and the steppe endures because no single defeat can shatter the whole.

advances.name: Horse Archer Tradition
advances.text: The composite bow and the steppe pony are the twin pillars of Kazakh warfare. From childhood, every nomad learns to shoot from horseback at full gallop, the famous Kazakh Shot, a rearward volley while retreating, that has broken many a pursuing army.

advances.name: Horse Breeding Mastery
advances.text:
The Kazakhs breed some of the hardiest horses in the world, compact, enduring animals that can survive on steppe grass alone. Wealthy bais own herds numbering in the tens of thousands, and the nation's equine wealth is the foundation of both its military power and its trade.

Available in: Steppe Horse Stud

advances.name: Aul Organization
advances.text:
The aul, the nomadic camp, is the basic unit of Kazakh society. Each aul moves with the seasons, following ancient migration routes between winter shelters and summer pastures. Their felt yurts can be raised in an hour and dismantled in less.

Available in: Aul Encampment

advances.name: Quriltay Tradition
advances.text:
In the Chinggisid tradition, the quriltay assembly gathers the clan elders, sultans, and military leaders to elect a khan, plan the year's migration, and allocate winter pastureland. It is the beating heart of steppe governance.

Available in: Quriltay Ground

advances.name: Legacy of the Yasa
advances.text: The Yasa of Genghis Khan, codified in 1206, remains the foundational legal tradition of the steppe. Its principles of collective responsibility, hierarchical command, and pastoral rights govern the relationship between khan and clan.

advances.name: Bonds of the Ru
advances.text: Every Kazakh knows their ru, their patrilineal clan, tracing seven generations of ancestors. These genealogical bonds transcend zhuz boundaries, binding the nation together through shared blood and obligation.

advances.name: Quriltay Guard
advances.text: The khan's personal retinue, chosen from the finest horsemen of every clan at the quriltay assembly. These mounted warriors serve as both bodyguard and shock cavalry, the sharp edge of the khan's authority.

advances.name: Silk Road Waystations
advances.text:
Along the caravan routes that cross the steppe, Kazakh waystations provide shelter, fresh horses, and provisions to traveling merchants. These posts connect the cities of Transoxiana to the markets of China and beyond.

Available in: Caravan Waystation

advances.name: Era of Kasym Khan
advances.text: Under Kasym Khan (r. 1509-1518), the Kazakh Khanate reached its peak, reportedly able to field two hundred thousand cavalry. His authority extended from the Irtysh to the Ural, and all neighboring powers feared the Kazakh horsemen.

advances.name: Steppe Horse Trade
advances.text: Kazakh horses are prized across Central Asia for their endurance, sure-footedness, and ability to thrive on sparse steppe forage. The trade in these animals is the khanate's most valuable commercial asset.

advances.name: Barymta Tradition
advances.text: Barymta, the ritualized livestock raid, serves as both economic redistribution and martial training. Young warriors prove themselves by seizing horses from rival clans, and the practice maintains the edge of nomadic cavalry skills between wars.

advances.name: Seasonal Migration
advances.text: The annual migration between zhailau (summer pastures) and kystau (winter camps) is the rhythm of nomadic life. This cycle maintains the grasslands, feeds the herds, and keeps the population spread across the territory, making the khanate remarkably resilient to invasion.

advances.name: Tore Lancers
advances.text: The Tore, the Chinggisid aristocracy, provide the heavy shock cavalry of the Kazakh army. These noble lancers, clad in mail and wielding long spears, lead the decisive charge that breaks enemy formations after the horse archers have softened them.

advances.name: Jeti Zhargy
advances.text:
The Seven Codes of Khan Tauke, assembled by the three great biys Tole, Kazybek, and Aiteke, codified the customary law of the Kazakh nation into a comprehensive legal framework governing inheritance, marriage, criminal justice, and pastoral rights.

Available in: Biy Court

event.title: The Jeti Zhargy
event.text:
In the twilight years of the seventeenth century, Khan Tauke assembled the three greatest biys of the Kazakh nation: Tole Bi of the Great Zhuz, Kazybek Bi of the Middle Zhuz, and Aiteke Bi of the Junior Zhuz. Together they codified the customary law of the steppe into the Jeti Zhargy, the Seven Codes.

These laws regulated everything from inheritance and marriage to livestock disputes and the punishment of crimes. They established the authority of the biy courts as the arbiters of justice across the vast steppe, binding diverse clans under a common legal framework without imposing centralized tyranny.

The Jeti Zhargy represents a choice: shall the law serve to strengthen the khan's authority over all disputes, or shall it enshrine the biys as the true pillars of governance?

options.text: The law strengthens the khan's hand

modifiers.name: Code of the Steppe
modifiers.text: The Jeti Zhargy has codified the customary law of the nomadic clans into a unified legal code, strengthening the khan's authority over disputes across the vast steppe.

options.text: The biys are the true voice of the steppe

modifiers.name: Authority of the Biys
modifiers.text: The Jeti Zhargy has enshrined the biy courts as the foundation of Kazakh justice, creating a decentralized system of governance that respects the autonomy of each zhuz while binding them under common law.

advances.name: Kumis Tradition
advances.text:
Kumis, fermented mare's milk, is the sacred drink of the steppe, served at every gathering from humble aul feasts to the quriltay itself. Its production is both a culinary art and an economic activity sustaining nomadic communities.

Available in: Kumis Brewery

advances.name: Three Zhuz Division
advances.text: The division of the Kazakh nation into the Great, Middle, and Junior Zhuz, each with its own territory, sultans, and traditions, is both the khanate's greatest vulnerability and its greatest strength. No single defeat can destroy a nation distributed across three autonomous hordes.

advances.name: Composite Bow Mastery
advances.text: The Kazakh composite recurve bow, layered from horn, sinew, and wood, delivers devastating power from horseback. Generations of refinement have made it lighter, more responsive, and more accurate, allowing the famous rearward Kazakh Shot at full gallop.

advances.name: Caravan Tolls
advances.text: Control of the steppe caravan routes allows the Kazakhs to levy tolls on Silk Road traffic passing through their territory. Merchants pay for safe passage, fresh mounts, and protection from bandits.

advances.name: Dzungar Mobilization
advances.text: The existential threat of the Dzungar invasion forced an unprecedented mobilization of the entire Kazakh nation. The zhasaq, tribal militia, was assembled by khan's decree, drawing every able-bodied man from the three zhuz to defend the homeland.

advances.name: Batyr Tradition
advances.text:
The batyr, the warrior champion, is the highest honor in Kazakh martial culture. Men like Bogenbai, Kabanbai, and Nauryzbai earned their title through feats of individual valor in battle, and their names echo through the centuries in epic poetry.

Available in: Batyr Training Ground

advances.name: Togan Guard Posts
advances.text: Unlike sedentary peoples who build walls, the Kazakhs defend their territory through mobile guard posts and watch stations along the frontier. These togan provide early warning of invasion and serve as rally points for the militia.

advances.name: Triumph at Anyrakay
advances.text: The forty-day battle at Anyrakay in 1730, where Abulkhair Khan's united Kazakh force shattered the Dzungar advance across two hundred kilometers of steppe, proved that nomadic cavalry coordinated across three zhuz could defeat any foe.

event.title: Triumph at Anyrakay
event.text:
For years the Dzungar Khanate had pressed westward, and the catastrophe of 1723, the Aktaban Shubyryndy, the Great Retreat, had nearly broken the Kazakh nation. Families scattered, herds were lost, and despair gripped the steppe.

But in the spring of 1730, the tide turned. Khan Abulkhair rallied thirty thousand warriors from all three zhuz, an unprecedented feat of unity. At Anyrakay, over forty days of fighting across two hundred kilometers of steppe, the legendary batyrs Bogenbai, Kabanbai, and Nauryzbai shattered the Dzungar advance. The invaders were expelled from Zhetysu, and the Kazakh people proved that the steppe could not be conquered.

This victory demands a decision: shall we press our advantage and pursue the Dzungars to their ruin, or consolidate what we have won and rebuild the solidarity of the three zhuz?

options.text: Pursue the retreating enemy. The steppe is ours

modifiers.name: The Steppe Resurgent
modifiers.text: The triumph at Anyrakay has unleashed the martial fury of the Kazakh nation. Emboldened by victory, our cavalry rides with renewed purpose, and the memory of our greatest batyrs inspires every warrior.

options.text: Rebuild and reunite. The zhuz must stand together

modifiers.name: Solidarity of the Zhuz
modifiers.text: The unprecedented unity of all three zhuz at Anyrakay has demonstrated that the Kazakh nation is strongest when it stands together. The bonds forged in common struggle now sustain a deeper mobilization.

advances.name: Horse-Silk Exchange
advances.text: The regulated trade between the Kazakh Khanate and the Qing Dynasty, exchanging hardy steppe horses for silk, tea, and manufactured goods. This became a pillar of diplomacy and a source of immense wealth for the Kazakh bais.

event.title: The Horse-Silk Exchange
event.text:
Between 1759 and 1796, the Qing emperor issued special decrees governing the horse trade with the Kazakh Khanate. The Kazakhs possessed what China needed most, hardy steppe horses by the tens of thousands, and China offered what the steppe desired: bolts of silk, tea, and manufactured goods.

This was no mere barter. The horse-silk exchange became a pillar of diplomacy, a regulated system of trade and tribute that enriched both empires. Kazakh bais grew wealthy beyond imagination, the legendary Aldan owned twenty-four thousand horses, while the nation's total herds numbered in the millions. The steppe had found a way to convert its boundless grasslands into enduring wealth.

options.text: The wealth of the steppe flows east and west

modifiers.name: Silk Road Wealth
modifiers.text: The regulated horse-silk exchange has transformed the boundless grasslands of the steppe into a source of enduring commercial wealth.

advances.name: Abulkhair's Diplomacy
advances.text: Khan Abulkhair of the Junior Zhuz navigated a perilous diplomatic landscape, seeking alliances with Russia against the Dzungars while attempting to preserve Kazakh sovereignty. His pragmatic statecraft set the template for steppe diplomacy in an age of great empires.

advances.name: Batyr Champions
advances.text: The ultimate expression of Kazakh martial tradition: legendary warriors who combine mastery of the composite bow, the lance, and horseback combat into a single devastating package. Their feats of arms inspire entire armies.

advances.name: Ablai Khan's Reforms
advances.text: Khan Ablai (r. 1771-1781) was the last khan to exercise real authority over all three zhuz. His diplomatic maneuvering between Russia and China, combined with centralizing internal reforms, represented the final flowering of the Kazakh Khanate as an independent power.

advances.name: Pastoral Wealth
advances.text:
At its peak, the Kazakh nation counted millions of horses, cattle, sheep, and camels. This livestock wealth, when properly managed and traded, rivals the silver mines and plantations of sedentary empires.

Available in: Livestock Market

advances.name: Nomadic Logistics
advances.text: Centuries of seasonal migration have given the Kazakhs an unmatched understanding of steppe logistics, the location of water sources, the carrying capacity of pastures, and the fastest routes across seemingly trackless grassland.

advances.name: Kazakh Warrior Code
advances.text: The codification of nomadic martial traditions, from the training of horse archers to the protocols of steppe warfare, preserves the fighting skills that have sustained the Kazakh nation through centuries of conflict.

advances.name: Steppe Resistance
advances.text:
The boundless steppe cannot be conquered by fortresses or supply lines. Every invading army that marches into the grasslands finds itself stretched thin, harried by mobile cavalry, and slowly consumed by the vastness itself.

Available in: Steppe Arsenal

advances.name: Zhyrau Poets
advances.text:
The zhyrau, wandering poet-sages who compose epic verse on the deeds of batyrs, the wisdom of biys, and the beauty of the steppe, are the keepers of Kazakh memory. Their oral tradition preserves the nation's history more faithfully than any archive.

Available in: Shezhire Archive

advances.name: Alash Identity
advances.text: Alash, the legendary ancestor of the Kazakh people, gives his name to the enduring sense of shared identity that binds the three zhuz together despite political fragmentation. In an age of encroaching empires, this cultural consciousness is the nation's ultimate defense.

advances.name: Livestock Modernization
advances.text: The application of new breeding techniques and veterinary knowledge to the vast Kazakh herds increases both the quality and quantity of livestock output, transforming pastoral nomadism into a more productive economic system.

advances.name: Zhuz Unity
advances.text: The growing awareness of shared Kazakh identity transcending zhuz boundaries lays the groundwork for a pan-Kazakh national consciousness, strengthening the bonds that hold the nation together against external pressures.

destiny.name: Destiny of the Kazakh Khanate
destiny.text: The Kazakh Khanate has risen from the ashes of the Uzbek confederation. Now the nation must choose its path, will it forge an empire of conquest or build enduring wealth across the boundless steppe?

conditions.text: Stability at least 25

event.title: Destiny of the Kazakh Khanate
event.text:
The Kazakh Khanate stands at the threshold of greatness. From the rolling grasslands of the Desht-i Kipchak to the snow-capped peaks of the Tian Shan, the descendants of Janibek and Kerei have built a nation. But a nation is not yet an empire, and the choices made now will determine whether the Kazakhs are remembered as conquerors or as the wisest stewards the steppe has ever known.

The path forward is ours to choose.

destiny.name: Cities of the Syr Darya
destiny.text: Reclaim the ancient Syr Darya cities of Sighnaq, Sawran and Otrar, the first seats of the Kazakh Khanate, and prove that the steppe's rightful rulers have returned.

conditions.text: Chose Legacy of Kasym Khan
Own Sighnaq, or a subject owns it
Own Otrar, or a subject owns it
Own Sawran, or a subject owns it
Stability at least 25

event.title: Cities of the Syr Darya
event.text:
Sighnaq, Sawran and Otrar, the ancient cities along the Syr Darya, have fallen under Kazakh dominion once more. These were the first seats of Kazakh power, where Janibek Khan held court and where the caravans of the Silk Road crossed paths with the nomadic hordes. Their reconquest marks the beginning of a greater ambition.

The walls of sedentary cities now shelter the khan's banners, and the world takes notice.

options.text: The first step on a long road

destiny.name: Conquest of Transoxiana
destiny.text: March south to seize the legendary cities of Samarkand and Bukhara, the jewels of the Timurid legacy. The Kazakh horsemen shall ride where Genghis and Timur once ruled.

conditions.text: Own Samarkand, or a subject owns it
Own Bukhara, or a subject owns it
Gold at least 2000
Prestige at least 50

event.title: Conquest of Transoxiana
event.text:
The unthinkable has been achieved. Kazakh cavalry rides through the streets of Samarkand, past the Registan and the turquoise domes of Timur's legacy. Bukhara, the Noble City, has opened its gates. The great oasis cities that once looked down upon the nomads of the steppe now pay tribute to a Kazakh khan.

This conquest demands a decision: shall we rule these cities with an iron fist, or harness their wealth through a more subtle arrangement?

options.text: The cities kneel before the steppe

modifiers.name: Timurids Humbled
modifiers.text: The conquest of Transoxiana demonstrates the supremacy of steppe cavalry over the garrison troops of sedentary cities. Mercenary companies flock to the khan's banner.

options.text: Let them pay tribute and keep their ways

modifiers.name: Oasis Tributaries
modifiers.text: Rather than destroying the wealth of the conquered cities, the khan extracts tribute through vassalage, accelerating the incorporation of new territories.

destiny.name: Empire of the Desht-i Kipchak
destiny.text: Unite the entire Kipchak steppe from the Volga to the Irtysh under Kazakh rule. Seize Astrakhan, the ruins of the Golden Horde capital at Sarai and Qashliq on the Irtysh, and restore the empire of Jochi Khan.

conditions.text: Own Astrakhan, or a subject owns it
Own Sarai, or a subject owns it
Own Khiva, or a subject owns it
Own Qashliq, or a subject owns it
Prestige at least 75

event.title: Empire of the Desht-i Kipchak
event.text:
From the banks of the Volga to the Irtysh at Qashliq, from Astrakhan to the ruins of Sarai where the Golden Horde once ruled, the entire Desht-i Kipchak now answers to a single khan. The Kazakh nation has achieved what no successor state of the Jochid Ulus managed since its collapse: the reunification of the western and eastern steppe under one banner.

This is more than conquest. This is the restoration of an empire that shook the world.

options.text: We are the heirs of Jochi Khan

modifiers.name: Successor of Jochi
modifiers.text: By claiming the legacy of Jochi Khan and the Golden Horde, the Kazakh Khanate commands the respect of all Turkic peoples and negotiates from a position of unassailable prestige.

options.text: We forge our own legacy upon the steppe

modifiers.name: Steppe Imperium
modifiers.text: A new empire rises on the steppe, not a restoration but something original. Conquered peoples are absorbed rapidly, and the khan's authority to wage war is recognized across the continent.

destiny.name: Silk Road Dominion
destiny.text: Control the city of Turkestan, the spiritual heart of the Kipchak steppe, and ensure that horses flow through Kazakh markets. Build the foundation of a pastoral trading empire.

event.title: Silk Road Dominion
event.text:
The sacred city of Turkestan, home to the shrine of Khoja Ahmed Yasawi, stands firmly within Kazakh hands. More importantly, the trade routes that crisscross the steppe now flow through Kazakh-controlled markets where horses, the true currency of the nomad, are traded in their tens of thousands.

The foundations of a pastoral commercial empire have been laid.

options.text: The wealth of the steppe flows through our hands

destiny.name: Pastoral Mastery
destiny.text: Secure Isfijab, fill the treasury and build up Turkestan, the seat of the khans. The wealth of millions of livestock shall rival any sedentary kingdom.

conditions.text: Own Isbijab, or a subject owns it
Gold at least 2000
We own Turkestan and its development is at least 18

event.title: Pastoral Mastery
event.text:
The Kazakh steppe economy has matured beyond simple pastoralism. Credit and coin now carry the trade in livestock and horses that once relied on barter alone. The city of Isfijab serves as a hub where nomadic wealth meets sedentary commerce, and Turkestan, where the khans hold court beside the shrine of Ahmad Yasawi, has grown at a pace that would astonish the khans of old.

Two paths of prosperity present themselves: shall we double down on the pastoral wealth that makes the steppe unique, or leverage our position as the indispensable link in the continental caravan trade?

options.text: The horse lords shall grow richer still

modifiers.name: Horse Lords
modifiers.text: The Kazakh bais control herds numbering in the millions. This pastoral wealth drives institutional development, though the reliance on livestock makes formal banking more costly.

options.text: The caravan routes are our true wealth

modifiers.name: Caravan Kings
modifiers.text: Kazakh control of the continental caravan routes creates a web of diplomatic connections and rapid recovery from disruption, though the focus on trade comes at the cost of military readiness.

destiny.name: The Boundless Steppe
destiny.text: Seize Chach, the gateway to Transoxiana's silk markets, build it into a great city and make the Kazakh economy a center of continental trade. The steppe shall know no limits.

event.title: The Boundless Steppe
event.text:
Chach, the gateway between the steppe and the silk-producing heartland of Central Asia, has been secured, and with it a flood of silk, tea, and precious goods pours into Kazakh markets. The nation has achieved what seemed impossible for a pastoral people: an economy that rivals any sedentary empire, built not on mines or plantations but on the boundless grasslands and the animals that sustain them.

The steppe has no walls, and neither does Kazakh ambition. A final choice remains: shall we concentrate this wealth into great cities, or spread it across the eternal pastures?

options.text: Build a metropolis worthy of the steppe

modifiers.name: Nomad Metropolis
modifiers.text: A great city rises on the steppe, a commercial and diplomatic hub where nomadic wealth is transformed into urban splendor, drawing merchants and envoys from across the continent.

modifiers.name: Eternal Pastures
modifiers.text: Rather than concentrating wealth in cities, the Kazakhs spread prosperity across the vast grasslands. Every estate thrives, the levy grows strong, and the steppe itself becomes the monument to Kazakh greatness.

units.name: Kazakh Horse Archers
units.text: The backbone of nomadic warfare: swift cavalry armed with composite recurve bows, masters of the feigned retreat and the devastating rearward volley.

units.name: Quriltay Guard
units.text: The khan's elite mounted retinue, chosen from the finest horsemen of every clan at the annual quriltay assembly.

units.name: Tore Lancers
units.text: Chinggisid noble cavalry wielding long lances, these heavy shock troops deliver the decisive charge that shatters enemy formations.

units.name: Zhasaq Militia
units.text: Tribal infantry mobilized by the khan's decree during times of existential threat, drawn from every able-bodied man across the three zhuz.

units.name: Batyr Champions
units.text: Legendary warrior champions who combine mastery of bow, lance, and horsemanship into an unmatched fusion of mobile striking power.

buildings.name: Steppe Horse Stud
buildings.text: Breeding grounds where the hardiest steppe horses are raised, compact, enduring animals that survive on grass alone and form the foundation of both Kazakh military power and trade wealth. Kept on the herd and horse pastures of the steppe.

children.text: The location's raw material is Livestock
The location's raw material is Horses

buildings.name: Quriltay Ground
buildings.text: A permanent assembly site where clan elders, sultans, and military leaders gather to elect khans, plan migrations, and settle disputes according to Chinggisid tradition.

buildings.name: Caravan Waystation
buildings.text: A Silk Road trading post providing shelter, fresh mounts, and provisions to merchants crossing the steppe, connecting the markets of Transoxiana to China.

buildings.name: Aul Encampment
buildings.text: The organized nomadic camp, the basic unit of Kazakh society, where felt yurts are raised along seasonal migration routes between zhailau and kystau.

buildings.name: Kumis Brewery
buildings.text: Facilities for the production of kumis, fermented mare's milk, the sacred drink of the steppe served at feasts, assemblies, and celebrations across the Kazakh nation.

buildings.name: Batyr Training Ground
buildings.text: A martial academy of the steppe where young warriors train in the arts of mounted archery, lance combat, and the feigned retreat under the guidance of veteran batyrs.

buildings.name: Biy Court
buildings.text: A judicial institution where biys, hereditary judges, settle disputes according to the Jeti Zhargy, the codified customary law of the Kazakh nation.

buildings.name: Frontier Watchtower
buildings.text: Guard posts along the steppe frontier providing early warning of invasion, serving as rally points for the militia, and imposing attrition on any invading force.

buildings.name: Khan's Chancellery
buildings.text: The administrative center of the khan's authority, where decrees are drafted, tribute is collected, and the affairs of the three zhuz are coordinated.

buildings.name: Livestock Market
buildings.text: A central trading hub where the vast herds of the Kazakh steppe are bought and sold, connecting pastoral producers with Silk Road merchants. Drovers bring their herds to it from far across the steppe.

buildings.name: Steppe Arsenal
buildings.text: A weapons depot maintaining stockpiles of bows, lances, sabers, and increasingly firearms for the defense of the Kazakh homeland.

buildings.name: Shezhire Archive
buildings.text: An institution dedicated to preserving the shezhire, the genealogical records and oral histories that form the backbone of Kazakh identity, through the work of zhyrau poet-sages.

buildings.name: Khan's War Camp
buildings.text: The mobile command center of the Kazakh khan during major campaigns, a sprawling complex of yurts, supply wagons, and corrals that serves as the nerve center of steppe warfare.

buildings.name: Great Bazaar
buildings.text: A vast permanent marketplace where the pastoral wealth of the steppe is traded alongside silk, spices, and manufactured goods from the sedentary world, the commercial heart of the Kazakh trading empire.

list.name: Jeti Jargy
list.text: In the closing decades of the seventeenth century Tauke Khan convened the three greatest biys (Tole Bi of the Senior Zhuz, Kazybek Bi of the Middle, Aiteke Bi of the Junior) and codified the customary law of the steppe into the Jeti Jargy, the Seven Codes. The codes regulate kun blood-money, bride-price, livestock theft, and the punishment of crimes; they enshrine the biy court as the steppe's true judicial authority. Where the codes are upheld, common Kazakhs find protection from arbitrary clan violence; where they decay, blood-feud and barymta cattle-raiding return.

list.name: The Three Zhuz
list.text: The genius of Kazakh governance after Kasym Khan lies not in the single khan but in the balance of three zhuz: the Ulu, or Senior, pasturing in Zhetysu; the Orta, or Middle, on the central steppe; and the Kishi, or Junior, along the Yaik. Each zhuz keeps its own pastures, its own biys, its own line of khans descended from Janibek and Kerei. Unity arises from consensus, never command. The arrangement makes the steppe nearly impossible to conquer, but each zhuz can and does treat with foreign powers independently, as Abulkhair did with Russia in 1731.

list.name: Ak-Suiek Tore
list.text: Kazakh society is rigidly bisected between Ak-Suiek (white bone) and Kara-Suiek (black bone). Only descendants of Chinggis Khan through Jochi, the Tore, may claim the title of khan or sultan; only Tore may speak in the Kuralay assembly with binding authority. Below them, Kara-Suiek clans are led by their own biys and batyrs but barred from sovereign office. The Tore caste gives the Kazakhs an unbroken chain of legitimate rule from Janibek to Kenesary, but their endogamous insularity hollows out the political role of the lesser clans.

funded.name: Horde Unity Change on Ruler Death

list.name: Aksakal Aul Governance
list.text: Below the khans and beyond the reach of any chancery, Kazakh nomadic life runs through the aul: a winter or summer camp of perhaps a dozen yurts belonging to a single extended kin group. The aksakal, the white-beard, is the senior elder whose word settles grazing rights, marriage contracts, and daily disputes that never reach a biy court. The institution has no building, no scroll, no salary; it operates wherever Kazakhs pitch their tents. When a khan demands more than the aul elders think just, the aul simply migrates beyond reach.

list.name: Batyr War Bands
list.text: Outside the formal Tore hierarchy stand the batyrs: warriors of any clan who have earned the title through deeds of arms. Bogenbai, Kabanbai, Nauryzbai: the names ring through Kazakh tradition as the men who broke the Dzungar invasion at Anyrakay in 1730 after the catastrophic Aktaban Shubyryndy retreat of 1723. A batyr commands a war-band drawn from his own kin and admirers; he answers to the khan only by choice, fights when there is honour or plunder to be had, and disperses when the campaign ends. The institution is the steppe's deepest reservoir of military manpower, but it runs on barymta and cannot be turned off when the campaign is done.
